courses.subject: ECLT
courses.title: E-Commerce and Logistics Technologies Internship

meetings.instructor:
Dr. PAN Hong, 
Professor GAO Xuefeng

courses.description:
The objective of the course is to allow students to acquire a basic understanding and the skills of the practical aspects of E-Commerce and Logistics Technologies. To qualify for the award of the subject credits, the student must attach to a company in an E-Commerce and Logistics Technologies related post as approved by the Professor-in-Charge for no less than 12 weeks. The student will have an academic supervisor as assigned by the Professor-in-Charge and an industry supervisor from the company. There will be a mid-term company visit by the academic supervisor. At the end of the internship, the student must give a presentation to the academic and industry supervisors, and submit a report summarizing what the student has done and learnt from the internship. The student's grade will be determined by (1) the presentation, (2) the student report and (3) a testimonial from the industry supervisor.

The internship should normally take place in the summer term after a student has finished the first two semesters of studies. Part-time students can decide to undertake the internship in the summer term of either the first or second year of studies.

Students are recommended to seek the Professor-in-Charge's comment on potential internship opportunities before enrolling in the course.

courses.subject: ECLT
courses.title: Supply Chain Analytics
courses.description:
This course provides a business-oriented introduction to the application of data analytics in optimizing supply chains. Students will explore accessible yet rigorous analytical concepts and techniques essential for data-driven decision-making in modern supply chain environments.

Throughout the course, students will gain hands-on experience with widely used and powerful software tools, enhancing their analytical proficiency. Lectures will cover key supply chain processes, including—but not limited to—demand and supply management, procurement and sourcing, inventory control and warehousing, route and transportation optimization, product returns and reverse logistics, and supply chain reliability under volatile trade relations.

Real-world case studies from diverse business contexts will be used to illustrate practical applications and deepen understanding.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students from MSc in E-Commerce and Logistics Technologies
courses.academic_group: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.academic_org: Div of System Erg & Erg Mgt
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. Apply Data Analytics for Supply Chain Optimization: Develop and implement data-driven strategies to enhance supply chain efficiency, reduce costs, and improve responsiveness using core analytics concepts and techniques.
2. Transform Data into Actionable Insights: Analyze complex datasets to generate meaningful insights that support informed decision-making in areas such as logistics, procurement, and inventory management.
3. Utilize Industry-Standard Analytical Tools: Gain hands-on experience with widely used and accessible data analytics software tools to perform real-time analysis, visualization, and modeling.
4. Address Key Supply Chain Functions: Tackle critical supply chain processes including demand forecasting, supply planning, procurement, inventory control, warehousing, transportation routing, reverse logistics, and risk management.
5. Understand Supply Chain Challenges Across Industries: Recognize and evaluate supply chain issues in diverse business environments, preparing to adapt analytical approaches to various operational contexts and sectors.
